title.title: Affine Bernstein: rigid through dimension 9, not in 10
title.subtitle: Claim: entire affine-maximal graphs are quadratic for $3 \le n \le 9$, and a smooth nonquadratic one exists for $n = 10$

plain: Must a certain endless, perfectly balanced surface be a simple bowl? Yes up to dimension nine, not in ten

object.axisLabel: the dimension $n$ of the graph's domain

beats.text: Chern asked: must an entire convex affine-maximal graph be quadratic?
The claim: yes in every dimension from 3 to 9, under Euclidean completeness
And a smooth nonquadratic graph in 10, so the answer flips exactly there

sources.quote: Chern's affine Bernstein problem (1977); Calabi (dim 2 with both completenesses); Trudinger-Wang (Invent. 2000): Euclidean-complete dim 2, reduction in all dims to a uniform strict-convexity modulus, and the singular dim-10 example
3 <= n <= 9, complete for the induced Euclidean metric, is an elliptic paraboloid (entire, quadratic)
Sharp: a smooth entire nonquadratic affine-maximal graph exists in R^10.
